children: U.S. export prices rose 0.6% M/M in August, vs. -0.2% consensus and -1.4% prior (revised from -1.3%), according to data released by the Bureau of Labor Statistics on Wednesday.
Prices for both nonagricultural exports and agricultural exports increased.
Year-over-year, export prices advanced 8.6% during the month, vs. +8.1% in July (revised from 8.2%).
Import prices were up 0.7% M/M vs. +0.3% consensus and -0.3% prior (revised from -0.4%). Higher prices for nonfuel imports more than offset lower prices for fuel imports.
Import prices advanced 7.0% from August 2025 to August 2026 (vs. +5.9% in July), the largest over-the-year increase since the index rose 7.7% in August 2022.

title: Export prices unexpectedly rise in August; import prices increase more than expected
